correctness.rationale: For tensor data the two-parameter truncated operator factors, so the principal-value limit is \(h_1(x)h_2(y)\). Compact support and the \(C^1\) homogeneous kernel give the uniform far-field expansion \(h_i(x)=M_iK_i(x)+O(|x|^{-d_i-1})\). After scaling, dominated convergence gives \(t\,|\{|h_i|>t\}|\to A_i=|M_i|d_i^{-1}\int|\Omega_i|\). The product distribution is then an exact layer-cake calculation: two index-one tails give \(A_1A_2\lambda^{-1}\log(1/\lambda)\), while the high-amplitude pieces are only \(O(\lambda^{-1})\) because one-parameter Calderón-Zygmund \(L^p\) boundedness gives the required truncated first moments. The proof explicitly excludes zero masses and does not infer the limit from finite experiments.
correctness.risk: The factorization of both kernel and input is essential; the argument does not address correlated angular variables or zero-mass cancellation.

final_claim: For a product of two smooth mean-zero homogeneous Calderón-Zygmund kernels and a compact tensor input with nonzero masses, the small-level distribution of the factorized product transform is asymptotic to \(C\lambda^{-1}\log(1/\lambda)\), with the exact coefficient \(C=|M_1M_2|(nm)^{-1}\|\Omega_1\|_{L^1(S^{n-1})}\|\Omega_2\|_{L^1(S^{m-1})}\).
limitations: Factorized kernels and tensor inputs only.
Both tensor-factor masses must be nonzero.
No second-order asymptotic or nonfactorized angular theorem is claimed.
